title: Threat Detection Library - Cisco Network Device Detection Entry
description: Schema for a single detection entry in data/cisco-detections.json. Like the ESXi/Splunk, Red Hat, Fortinet, Dell iDRAC, HPE iLO, Windows DHCP/RDP, VCF, Splunk Platform, and Active Directory catalogues, these entries are authored for this project rather than sourced from a single upstream project -- but this catalogue was built with a specific, documented methodology: every entry closes a gap identified by diffing this library against data/mitre-attack-cisco.json (MITRE ATT&CK's official Detection Analytics for the 'Network Devices' platform -- the ATT&CK platform value that covers Cisco IOS/IOS XE/ASA/FTD router, switch, and firewall techniques; MITRE does not define a separate 'Cisco' platform). Every entry's mitre_analytics[] field cites the specific official MITRE Detection Analytic ID(s) it is grounded in, the same provenance pattern used by the original ESXi catalogue's MITRE-driven gap-fill batch. Several entries additionally cite a real, MITRE-documented Cisco-targeting campaign or malware family (SYNful Knock, the ArcaneDoor campaign's Line Dancer/Line Runner, Salt Typhoon's JumbledPath, KV Botnet Activity) where the technique maps directly to one.

id.description: Namespaced sequential ID, one namespace per primary MITRE tactic -- the same fifteen-namespace convention the Splunk ESCU catalogue uses.

component.description: 'Cisco IOS/IOS XE' for router/switch-specific behavior (ROMMON, boot images, IOS CLI), 'Cisco ASA/FTD' for firewall-specific behavior (ASA/Firepower Threat Defense, including the ArcaneDoor campaign's Line Dancer/Line Runner-relevant techniques), or generic 'Cisco Network Device' for behavior that applies across the device family (AAA/TACACS+, SNMP, syslog integrity, generic CLI/config).

detection_type.description: Uses the same TTP/Anomaly/Hunting/Correlation vocabulary as the Splunk ESCU catalogue, since this catalogue is built from the same MITRE Detection Analytic source material.

mitre_analytics.description: Provenance link(s) to the official MITRE ATT&CK Detection Analytic(s) (data/mitre-attack-cisco.json) this entry is grounded in -- same field shape as the ESXi catalogue's MITRE-driven gap-fill batch (id = the analytic's ANnnnn identifier, name = its parent Detection Strategy's descriptive name, which is far more legible in the UI than the analytic's own generic 'Analytic nnnn' name).

threat_reference.description: Optional citation to a real, MITRE-documented Cisco-targeting campaign, intrusion set, or malware family this technique is directly associated with (e.g. SYNful Knock, ArcaneDoor/Line Dancer/Line Runner, Salt Typhoon/JumbledPath, KV Botnet Activity).
